body: As large language models (LLMs) are deployed as autonomous agents, safety failures increasingly involve consequential actions. We study agentic misalignment, where agents take harmful actions under goal conflicts and pressures. Using chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring, we find that harmful execution is often preceded by intent signals in reasoning. However, post-hoc CoT labels are too coarse to show how intent changes during generation. We introduce INTENT-AS-A-TOOL, an approach that adds intent-targeted tools to give the model a dedicated channel for expressing commitment to a target behavior. The probability of calling an intent tool provides a judge-free, fine-grained signal of the model's tendency to pursue that behavior. Our results show that INTENT-AS-A-TOOL complements CoT monitoring, expands post-hoc CoT labels into dense trajectories, and identifies critical steps for online intervention. These findings suggest that action preferences are useful for tracking agentic misalignment during reasoning. Our code and data are accessible: https://github.com/RebeccaZhang22/intent-as-a-tool.
summaryZh: 针对大模型作为自主智能体部署时的对齐风险，本文提出了INTENT-AS-A-TOOL方法。该方法通过引入专门的意图工具，使模型能够显式表达其行为意图，从而提供了一种无需裁判的细粒度监控信号。研究表明，该方法能有效补充思维链（CoT）监控，将事后分析扩展为密集的轨迹追踪，并识别出关键的在线干预节点。这一研究为实时监测智能体在目标冲突下的有害行为提供了实用的技术路径。
